abstract: KRAS is a GTPase regulating key signalling processes involved in cell proliferation, differentiation, growth and survival. KRAS is the most prevalent oncogene in human cancers, often acquiring a point mutation at Glycine 12 (G12). Although several possible amino acid substitutions occur at this hotspot in humans, most animal cancer models often examine only a single or limited subset of G12X variants, restricting our understanding of their distinct biological effects. Here, we describe a novel transgenic toolkit in Drosophila melanogaster comparing the most frequently observed oncogenic G12X variants (G12A, G12C, G12D, G12R, G12S, G12V), and evaluate these across multiple developmental and tumour contexts in vivo. Interestingly, we demonstrate how the phenotypic strength of each G12X variant differs significantly depending on the biological context, highlighting the importance of considering these point mutations systematically. Overall, our comprehensive RasG12X toolkit provides a powerful and versatile platform to explore the dysregulation of KRAS in vivo, serving as a valuable resource enabling unprecedented opportunities to investigate variant- and context-specific mechanisms of oncogenic signalling with direct relevance to cancer biology and therapy.
